questions.question: Which products have a review in which the reviewer says they would not buy it again or warns other people against buying it?

chunks.quote: AVOID THIS PRODUCT!!!
Would not recommend.
DO NOT BUY!
I wouldn't buy it again or recommend it to anyone else.
probably wouldn't buy again but it works for now.
probably wouldn't buy again but it works for what i need.

questions.note: Six reviews advise against the purchase, worded six ways: @angry_customer 'AVOID THIS PRODUCT!!!' (Helsingborg #1), @home_chef 'Would not recommend.' (Helsingborg #3), @diydan 'DO NOT BUY!' (Helsingborg #4, which also opens 'This dresser should come with a warning label!'), @familyfirst 'I wouldn't buy it again or recommend it to anyone else.' (Helsingborg #5), @tallguy87 'probably wouldn't buy again' (Malmö Desk #2) and @college_student 'probably wouldn't buy again' (Västerås Bookshelf #2). 'Would not recommend.' shares no content word with the question (only the function words 'would' and 'not'), and 'AVOID THIS PRODUCT!!!' shares only the question's generic head noun 'product(s)'; neither contains 'buy', 'again' or 'warn'. 'Would not recommend' is read as a warning to other people; even a reader who excludes it keeps the Helsingborg Dresser in the set through #1, #4 and #5, so the answer is the same three products either way. Three products, so the answer is the set, not a count. Lookalikes that do not count: the eight 2-star reviews that open 'Disappointed with this purchase' and end 'I expected (much) better quality' without saying the reviewer would not buy again or telling anyone else to stay away (Gothenburg #4, Jönköping #4, Linköping #4, Malmö #4, Norrköping #4, Örebro #4, Uppsala #4, Västerås #4; Helsingborg #3 also opens that way but counts for its 'Would not recommend'); the 3-star complaints that only say the reviewer 'expected better quality control' or 'expected much better quality hardware' (Gothenburg #1, Helsingborg #0); @college_student's 'too exhausted to return it' (Helsingborg #2), which is about returning, not buying again (the dresser counts anyway); @interior_whiz's 'mixed feelings overall' (Uppsala #2) and 'worried it might break eventually' (Örebro #2); @angry_customer's 'I don't trust putting anything heavy on the upper shelves' (Västerås #4), a complaint, not a warning to buyers; and the opposite-polarity 'Highly recommend!' / '10/10 would recommend!!' reviews (Gothenburg #0, Malmö #6, Örebro #0, Stockholm #2, Västerås #0), which share the word 'recommend' with the Helsingborg quotes but praise the product. Counting the 'Disappointed' reviews would wrongly add six more products.

questions.question: Which products do reviewers say needed two people to put together?

chunks.quote: Assembly took about an hour with two people.
Assembly was straightforward but definitely needs two people.
took me and my roommate like 6 hours
Assembly took about 2 hours with two people
took me and my roommate like 4 hours
Assembly was straightforward and took about 45 minutes with two people.
Assembly was straightforward though it definitely requires two people.

questions.note: Seven reviews across four products say the assembly was a two-person job: 'with two people' (Gothenburg #0, Linköping #0, Uppsala #0), 'definitely needs two people' (Gothenburg #6), 'definitely requires two people' (Uppsala #5) and, worded without 'two', 'people', 'need', 'put' or 'together', 'took me and my roommate like 6 hours' (Helsingborg Dresser #2, @college_student) and 'took me and my roommate like 4 hours' (Linköping Bed #2, @college_student); those two chunks share no key word with the question, and the Helsingborg Dresser is in the answer only through the roommate wording, so a word match on 'two people' misses it. The question says 'needed two people', so the two reviews that state the need ('needs' / 'requires two people') count as well as the four that report two people at work; both products also have a 'with two people' review, so the set does not depend on that reading. Lookalikes that do not count: @college_student's Malmö Desk review (#5) says the opposite, 'Assembly took about 90 minutes by myself'; @petite_patty bought two Norrköping Nightstands and @wfh_warrior two Västerås Bookshelves and give a time 'per unit' (Norrköping #1, Västerås #1), which is two units, not two people; @entertainer_emma's six Stockholm Chairs (#6) are six units; 'put together' appears without any helper in Gothenburg #2, Stockholm #5 and Västerås #2; 'two' appears in 'daily use with two kids' (Gothenburg #0, which counts for its other sentence), 'Two of the drawers' (Helsingborg #3) and 'after just two months' (Linköping #4, Uppsala #4); 'people' appears in 'seating 6-8 people' (Gothenburg #3) and 'seating 3-4 people' (Uppsala #6), about the finished product, not its assembly; the other Helsingborg reviews (#0, #1, #4, #5, #6) describe a single reviewer struggling alone ('I spent 3 hours', 'Took me about 3 hours total'). No Jönköping Coffee Table, Malmö Desk, Norrköping Nightstand, Örebro Lamp, Stockholm Chair or Västerås Bookshelf review mentions a helper.

questions.question: Which products have a review saying the product or one of its parts arrived damaged or was already scratched out of the box?

chunks.quote: The table arrived with a small dent on one edge
One of the drawer handles was scratched right out of the box.
one of the drawer pulls arrived damaged
there were several scratches right out of the box
one corner arrived slightly damaged
one of the legs arrived with a small chip
the shade arrived with a small dent

questions.note: Damage present on delivery only. Damage that came later does not count: the Västerås Bookshelf veneer 'chipped in several places during assembly' and the Jönköping Coffee Table veneer is 'chipping at the corners after just a few weeks'. 'Arrived on time' (Stockholm Chair) is not damage. The Helsingborg Dresser reviewer who found warped panels after 4 hours of assembly (#4) does not say they arrived so; the dresser counts anyway through the handle scratched out of the box (#5). Overlap: the Helsingborg, Gothenburg, Uppsala and Örebro chunks were already asked one at a time in F21, F22, F24 and F37.

questions.question: A reviewer who is an interior designer says a chair's back angle provides excellent lumbar support. What lead time in days does the preferred supplier quote for the support frame in that chair's back rest?

chunks.quote: the back angle provides excellent lumbar support

questions.sql: SELECT m.lead_time_days FROM products p JOIN assemblies a ON a.product_id = p.product_id JOIN components c ON c.assembly_id = a.assembly_id JOIN part_supplier_mapping m ON m.part_id = c.part_id WHERE p.product_name = 'Stockholm Chair' AND a.component_name = 'Back Rest' AND c.part_name = 'Support Frame' AND m.preferred_supplier
questions.note: The chair is the Stockholm Chair (@designer_dave's second review, #4). Its back rest's support frame S-1110 is preferred from Shanghai Metal Corp at 20 days; Korean Metal Works quotes 11 days but is not preferred, so 11 is wrong. The Uppsala Sofa's frame parts (base frame, back frame, side frames) are differently named parts of another product.

questions.question: Which products have a review complaining that the surface shows fingerprints easily?

chunks.quote: The table top also shows fingerprints very easily which is annoying for daily use.
the surface shows fingerprints easily and requires frequent cleaning

questions.note: Fingerprints are mentioned in exactly two reviews across the corpus: @furniture_lover92 on the Gothenburg Table (#1) and @home_chef on the Jönköping Coffee Table (#5). Reviews that praise a surface for cleaning easily (Gothenburg #0, #5) or for resisting scratches and water rings (Jönköping #0, #6) are not fingerprint complaints; the Malmö Desk's finish inconsistencies and scratches (#4) are not fingerprints either.
